Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on this recording, so just call me the driver of the gray sedan.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision occurred?
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Pasadena, Texas, in the right-hand lane.
Q: What happened next?
A: The light was red and I had been sitting there for a few seconds. Then I felt a hard impact from behind. My head
snapped forward and my car was pushed into the intersection.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: No. I was looking at the light and I didn't check my mirror. I only heard the brakes at the last second.
Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle?
A: Yes, but my left arm hurt badly. I held my wrist against my chest while I waited for the ambulance.
Q: Where were you taken for treatment?
A: I was taken by ambulance to a local hospital. They took X-rays and told me the wrist was fractured. I now have a
cast and I've been told I may need a follow-up with a hand specialist.
Q: Did you notice any other injuries?
A: My neck and upper back were stiff the next morning, and I had a headache for several days.
Q: Has anyone else been in contact with you about the accident?
A: Only a tow company and the police officer who came to the scene.
Q: Is tehre anything you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I was stopped and waiting for the light when this happened. I'd like my repair and medical costs to be
handled promptly.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>
